item.title: Re: Radio Virus SCP seeking green light
item.content:encoded:
Thank you very much for your critique. It really means a lot. The Announcer is responsible for the horde, but not aware of the hordes existence or his part in making it. This story is about what happens when a version of him finally learns about the true nature of himself and his “siblings”. As for the connection between the man and beast, it’s symbolic of having a dream fulfilled that a person thought they wanted, but the reality was a lot different than what they’d expected. As for in-universe explanation, the creatures are the enforcers, making sure that the Virus spreads by blocking out every other sound.

I hope that at least answers some of your questions. Have a happy holiday season.

item.title: Re: Radio Virus SCP seeking green light
item.content:encoded:
Was asked to take a look at this.

Can you explain the connection between the radio announcer and the horde idea? Like, I'm not sure what the take-away is here — 1930s radio announcers are getting out of control?

This seems like a very character-centric story but I don't feel like I have a handle on who the announcer character is. Is he aware of or responsible for the horde thing? What's going on?

In addition I recommend you use tropes like brainwashing and compulsion effects carefully, they tend to be easily understandable by your audience since they've seen them a dozen times, and thereof lose their novelty quickly.

item.title: Re: Radio Virus SCP seeking green light
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the critique. It really means a lot to me.

To answer some of your questions, I did mean that the host overwrites the mind of the listener, but I didn’t put that down for some reason, probably going to change that later. And to clarify about the monsters, it is both physically and psychologically transformed into a slender man/wendigo type monster with the ability to cancel out most noises. I’m still trying to work out the center so narrative, but your feedback has given me a lot of inspiration for what I can do with this idea.

Thank you so much for taking your time to help me with this. I know how many emails you probably get in a day, so I’m honored you chose mine. I wish you happiness

item.title: Re: Radio Virus SCP seeking green light
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Central narrative:

What I'm really looking for out of a central narrative section is 'what does the article contain': you've mostly used it to expand on what the SCP does; and I'm left wondering what the Foundation's role in all this is and like…what the actual article would look like.

Like bear in mind: you're trying to write a short story about a weird thing disguised as a technical report; not an encyclopedia entry on it; and so what you do with the SCP is a lot more important than just what the SCP can do.

each mind-swap creates a copy of the host of the radio show.

"mind-swap" implies "the listener and the host swap minds"; but it seems like you mean "the host overwrites the listener's mind" here?

Once they spread the virus, they turn into ruthless monsters.

Why do they turn into ruthless monsters? What does this look like? Like is it a psychological change? A physical change? Both?

Really my concern here is that it feels like it'd be a lot more interesting to look at what happens when there's this growing hive mind of radio hosts than tacking on a thing about them becoming monsters at the end; but perhaps there's a fun angle where some part of the hive mind growth causes it to happen and the story is almost…tragedy-like in style, y'know? It's like, us slowly watching a character we like turn from being cool and nice to a radio host to a rabid monster, y'know? As a like commentary on how e.g. stuff like fox news affects people say.

item.title: Radio Virus SCP seeking green light
item.content:encoded:
Seeking green light: yes

Page type: SCP article

Elevator pitch: A radio talk show that over-writes listener’s minds with a copy the show’s host consciousness.
Each victim has the innate desire to broadcast their voice over radio, creating more of these anomalous talk shows to infect more people. After they do this, they transform into blood thirsty monsters, both physically and psychologically, who have the ability to cancel out sounds within a certain radius of them, excluding the actual radio virus.

Central narrative: The Foundation has partial containment of the SCP, with a few instances still at large. The article will also contain an interview with a person who’s mind was over-written, as well as an account of said person going through all three stages of the disease.

Hook: it’s a audio memetic virus that transforms the victim into a copy of a 1930’s talk show host who may not have even existed, connected to a hive mind of other victims. Once they spread the virus, they turn into ruthless monsters.

Additional thoughts: I don’t know if this is a unique enough concept to be made official. I would really appreciate any critiques you have to make. This is my first entry and I’m exited to share my ideas with you.

Edits: since this threads creation, I have completely overhauled the central narrative part and expanded on the elevator pitch. My thanks to cybersqyd for critiquing the original article.
